## 5. An exact result for the full mean: polynomial input conditioning

For the actual all-minus first-passage mean,
\[
\boxed{
|\partial_\theta\log T_h|\le4n,\qquad
|\partial_{\beta h}\log T_h|\le2n.
}
\]
Hence
\[
\left|\log\frac{T_h(\theta',\phi')}{T_h(\theta,\phi)}\right|
\le
4n|\theta'-\theta|+2n|\phi'-\phi|.
\]

This follows by differentiating the killed Poisson equation and using the positivity supplied by the ordered current.

Thus exponentially long occurrence times do **not** force exponentially precise inputs. \(O(\log(n/\epsilon))\) fractional bits in the dimensionless parameters suffice for relative error \(O(\epsilon)\), in addition to representing \(R\).

## 6. Exact limitation

The requested full confidence interval has **not** been constructed.

The missing operation is physical, entropy-preserving transport through unrestricted principal contours, together with its composition through growth. In particular, the present construction does not yet control all significant channels involving multiple cut crossings, long irreducible junctions, remote contacts, and repeated creation or removal of principal holes.

The failed cap decoder, corrected-word coupling, overhang simplification, and Boolean pure-growth dual are preserved as explicit counterexamples or failed proof routes. None is being treated as evidence that the desired predictor is impossible.

The strongest unconditional full-mean algorithm retained so far still costs
\[
\operatorname{poly}_\theta
(n,R,\epsilon^{-1},\log\delta^{-1})\,e^{C_\theta R}.
\]

The completed advance is the explicit relative residence certificate (3), supported by acquired thermal redistribution, weighted phase-domain pruning, and actual-target completion. It removes the need to simulate a substantial class of long repairs, but it does not yet remove the exponential factor from prediction of the full transition mean.
